title: SWE-1.7: HARNESS-NATIVE
lede: July 8, 2026. The crossover point: a model trained directly inside the Devin agent harness, on tasks long enough that a single rollout blows past the context window. SWE-1.7 was the lab's first claim to frontier-level intelligence — at a fraction of frontier-level cost.
body:
h2. TRAINED WHERE IT WORKS

p. Every SWE model before this one was trained %(ok)for% a harness. SWE-1.7 was trained %(hl)inside% one. The Devin agent loop — plan, act, observe, retry — became the RL environment itself, which is a different claim than 'evaluated in Devin': the gradient went through the real thing.

h2. THE TWO PROBLEMS LONG-HORIZON RL BRINGS

* %(cyan)Context exhaustion% — Devin tasks run long enough that rollouts exceed the raw context window; training had to teach the model to work beyond what it can literally see.
* %(cyan)Reasoning bloat% — RL on reasoning tasks tends to inflate response lengths (the DeepSeek R1 effect). SWE-1.7 was trained to %(amber)elaborate only when the task is hard%, keeping routine work cheap.

h2. THE HISTORICAL FOOTNOTE

p. SWE-1.7's most durable contribution to the archive may be as a %(amber)baseline%. Two months later, the SWE-2 announcement measured itself against this model: 58% fewer turns, 81% lower cost, first code edit at step 18 instead of step 48. Every artifact in a museum eventually becomes the ruler a newer artifact is measured with.

bq. From the start, we built Devin for completing asynchronous, long-running tasks. SWE-1.7 is trained directly in the Devin harness. %(dim)— Cognition, July 2026%

p. Final hall: "SWE-2":swe-2.html — the model this lineage was rehearsing for.
